titre: Agents enter design systems and learn when to stop

syntheses.titre: Design systems now need to be readable by agents
syntheses.texte: Érica Menin starts from a simple observation: our design systems have a not-so-new consumer, AI agents, and she is beginning to make them usable by those agents. Figma is moving in the same direction with Specs, a markdown medium on the canvas presented as a context container. MCP and GitHub bring this context in and out. Written documentation thus becomes the interface between the designer and the agent.

syntheses.titre: Designing agent permissions is becoming a real design topic
syntheses.texte: Lisa Demchenko takes the example of a product that shows its plan before acting on your files and keeps changes reversible. From it she draws a permission model: what will change, why the agent is asking, that the action can be undone, and a calm way to decline. For her these are design decisions, and she wants to see more designers in these discussions.

syntheses.titre: MCP connects AI to tools and moves context around
syntheses.texte: Figma presents MCP as a way to move context to and from the canvas, with a reply asking whether an agent could write back into a Spec. A LinkedIn post sums up the idea in terms of roles: a connected tool gives AI a team function, including a "Product Designer" via Figma. The focus is shifting from the tool to the context you feed it.
